newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduran defense minister says his job is useless.
newsitem.headline: Honduran defense minister says his job is useless.

text.p: Honduras' defence minister said on Thursday he thought his post should be scrapped because he had no control over the armed forces.
Col. Jose Nunez, appointed by President Carlos Reina in 1996 over the objections of top officers, told reporters the country's military commanders did not listen to him.
"Really I don't think the post of defence minister should exist in Honduras. I have no position of authority in the armed forces," Nunez said.
Honduras' defence minister has traditionally been an intermediary between the chief of the armed forces and the civilian president.

But in appointing Nunez, Reina passed over higher-ranking officers suggested for the post by the military top brass. It was an unprecedented snub in a country where the armed forces has traditionally had considerable political power.

Nunez was replying to questions about recent tensions between Honduras and El Salvador about illegal logging in Honduras. He said military chiefs had reported on the situation directly to the president.

"I do not give out information but it's mostly because I do not have access to information," Nunez said. "(My role) is to simply sign the monthly budget for the armed forces and from time to time sign permits for people to carry weapons."
